current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 104 of them on 2 October 2026: 36 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; the Half-Life demo does not load a connectome at all by default, and DesktopFly mostly switches coded animations. No fly has been "uploaded". This week's fastest-growing claim, "I put a fly's brain into Terraria. And tried to train it" (28,244 views on 2 Oct 2026), is graded B: its open code really runs a MaleCNS connectome with learning synapses through hand-mapped senses and muscles, but there is no control. "I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (623,504 views) still names no model, data or code and stays U. Who does the walking in a "fly brain learned to walk" video? In our own pre-registered test, the Shiu et al. whole-brain model drove the FlyGym fly through a rate-to-drive mapping we wrote by hand: with its forward-walking neurons (P9) stimulated, the fly walked 13.9 mm in 1 s with the real brain, 14.1 mm with a scrambled brain and 14.3 mm with no brain. The legs, rhythm and balance come from FlyGym's controller; the brain sends two numbers every 100 ms; our mapping caps them, so speed could hardly differ by construction. The real brain did add turning commands (DNa02) that scrambled brains did not, and a brain tasting sugar sent no walking command at all. One stimulus, one model, one body, 1 s, open loop. Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 25 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir, ML and our walking tests it tied or lost (8). The answer depends on how the wiring is scrambled: in our own pre-registered test of the sugar reflex, degree-preserving and weight shuffles silenced the feeding motor neuron MN9 (0 Hz against 85.2 Hz), scrambling only the interior wiring kept 46%, and sign shuffles made the whole brain fire; stronger synapses never brought MN9 back, but no gain matched the real activity on 3 shuffles, so by our unchanged rules that row scores mixed, unfair and weak. Even where wiring helps, a brainless baseline often matches the fly: in Doom the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s and a brainless autopilot 51.93 s, and across 15 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 2. Only 10 of 33 control studies are methodologically strong, the other numbers are the authors' own and none is replicated. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove MN9 to 85.2 Hz and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz; on 2 Oct 2026 we also tested connecting it to a FlyGym body.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 104 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 36 you can try online, 52 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 20 viral claims, 33 control studies, and our own tests, including who does the walking when a fly brain drives a body.

summary: 104 entries checked on 2 Oct 2026 (4 new in the sixth check): 22 grade A, 21 B, 24 C, 4 D, 9 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded).

Who does the walking? (made by us, pre-registered on 2 Oct 2026 before the first trial): the Shiu et al. FlyWire v783 model with its forward-walking neurons P9 (DNp09) stimulated at 150 Hz drove FlyGym 2.1.0's two-number walking drive through our hand-made mapping. Forward distance in 1 s: real brain 13.93 ± 0.58 mm (3 seeds), scrambled brain 14.15 mm (3 degree-preserving shuffles that sent identical drives, in effect one walk), no brain with a constant drive 14.28 mm, no brain with random drives 13.96 ± 0.46 mm, zero drive 0 mm.

What the brain sends: tasting sugar fires MN9 at 82 Hz while every walking command neuron stays at 0 Hz, so the fly stands. P9 fires because we stimulate it, at the same rates in real and scrambled brains. Only the real wiring recruits the turning neurons DNa02 (right 21-29 Hz > left 7-11 Hz in all 3 seeds); no trial sent a backward command (MDN). In 1 s the resulting heading changes (-0.4 to -26 degrees) are within what random brainless drives produce (-7 to -27).

Limits of the body test: our mapping caps each drive number at 1.2 and 90 of the 120 drive values of the P9 walks sit at the cap, so forward speed could hardly differ by construction; one stimulus, one model, one body, 1 s, open loop; the turning sign of P9 was changed before the first body run to match Bidaye et al. 2020.

Controls ledger: 33 studies, 25 with a wiring null: helps 10, no difference 6, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1. New: our body test (no difference, fair, strong by the fixed rules; disclosed: its 3 shuffles sent identical drives). No scoring rule changed; two display-only arm fields (activity_ratio, activity_class) were added and never enter a score.

Our 1 Oct fair test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz (5 each); boundary-preserving 39 ± 1.22 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 ± 43 Hz with the whole brain ignited (activity runaway, 258 times real). Gain check finished on 2 Oct: x2.5 matched shuffle 3 but not shuffles 4 and 5, so not matched on 3 shuffles; MN9 stayed at 0 Hz at every gain (0.37 to 2.12 times the real activity). The row stays mixed, unfair and weak.

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 15 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control, commit 6b22922) the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s, a brainless autopilot 51.93 s and the best of 12 autopilot settings 53.44 s. fly-cartpole, now read at commit 077dcba: 392.5 vs 390.3 steps for shuffled wiring (p = 0.48); a TD learner reaches the 500-step ceiling.

"I put a fly's brain into Terraria. And tried to train it" (George Ostrobrod, 0nniju8lLxk; 28,244 views on 2 Oct 2026): grade B from the GitLab code at 9052966d (older than the video). A checksummed MaleCNS v1.0 connectome with reward-modulated plasticity drives a Terraria body through hand-mapped sensory and motor populations; we recomputed its 176-life log (median 102.8 s first 44 lives vs 163.3 s last 44, p = 0.037); no plasticity-off or scrambled-wiring control.

"I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (623,504 views on 2 Oct 2026) and a Roblox fight video (141,595): both grade U, no code. Pokémon on a Raspberry Pi and the Rainbow Six Siege claim: still U.

New entries: a hidden attractor in the Shiu et al. model (A: about 8,100 neurons keep firing for 10 s after a strong sugar pulse, also in the original Brian2 code), the Terraria fly (B), a leg-wiring study with six rewired families whose results are not public yet (B, provisional), and a FlyGym + BANC v888 bridge (C, a derivative, not a download lure).

The choice of null changes answers: in flyconnectome-nulls standard nulls beat the connectome (1.78 and 1.77 vs 1.57) but boundary-keeping nulls tie it (1.58 and 1.62); in our own reflex test four nulls give silent, partly and runaway; in our walking test the readout (our capped mapping) left the wiring little room to matter.

36 entries have a no-install link; all answered our HTTP check on 2 Oct 2026 (2 after a redirect), but none was played by us. FlyDoom (eganeganegan) returned HTTP 404 on 1 and 2 Oct 2026; its record is kept.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones, the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo and the Roblox maze race get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default.
Video gallery (2 Oct 2026): 52 videos, 46 of them original uploads; 34 of 104 catalogue entries have at least one video. Thumbnails unchanged.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own: tested 28 Sep 2026 and re-tested 1 Oct 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz real, 0 Hz shuffled; 82.0 Hz bit-exact). The deeper path Add a body is tested since 2 Oct 2026: brain tested (Python 3.11), body tested (uv, CPython 3.12.11, flygym 2.1.0, MUJOCO_GL=disable; set TMPDIR to a folder with about 400 MB free), mapping ours; FlyGym 2.0 rewrote the interface, so 1.x code does not run unchanged.
uncertainty: Our body test covers one stimulus (P9 at 150 Hz on both sides), one brain model, one body, 1 s of open-loop walking, 3 trial seeds and 3 shuffles that sent identical drives. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours: it caps the drive at 1.2, so another mapping could let the wiring matter more. The pre-registered P9 sign, other P9 rates and other descending neuron types were not tested in the body.

Our fair test covers one reflex (sugar to MN9) in one model, with one 1 s trial per shuffle at one trial seed; the MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition. The gain-matched arm is not matched on 3 shuffles; a per-shuffle gain search has not been run.

No demo was played in a real browser; "page responds" is an HTTP check only. YouTube watch pages refused our requests on 2 Oct 2026 (HTTP 429), so the Terraria description was not re-read and view counts come from search pages; the Terraria, Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight videos were not watched.
The Terraria verdict rests on code older than the video; fly-walking-wiring's B is provisional because its results are not public.

Controls ledger: every number except our own two tests is the authors'. We recomputed 15 studies from their committed files but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 33 are peer-reviewed. Only 10 of 33 studies reach "strong" method quality; 18 are weak.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. Our body test scores strong although its 3 shuffles behaved as one; our reflex test is "mixed" by rule although its arms read silent, partly and runaway. We did not override the rules for our own rows. Activity fields are reported only for our two tests. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale. The flyvis ablation values were not extracted.

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls have been applied to one reflex (ours: 46% kept), not to the other reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect beyond its commit subjects.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of some records were reused from earlier checks and are labelled with those dates in projects.json.
Not yet triaged: about 30 new low-star repositories from this week, three small repositories deferred twice, leads deferred in earlier weeks, and about 211 repositories listed only in directories.

Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated. The attractor reported for the Shiu et al. model has not been reproduced by us.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. Add a body is tested on Linux CPU only, without rendering. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.
Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
